notes.text: On which, &c. — That is, by, or before which, they were to present their prayers to God for counsel and succor upon all occasions. And this is mentioned here as the reason why David put himself and his people to so great trouble and charge, because it was to fetch up the choicest treasure which they had.

They set, &c. — Being taught, and encouraged to do so, by the example of the Philistines, who did so without any token of God's displeasure upon them for so doing. But they did not sufficiently consider, that God might wink at the Philistines, because they were ignorant of God's laws; and yet be angry with them for the same thing, because they knew, or might have known the law of God, which commanded the priests to bear it upon their shoulders. But their present transports of joy of the happy change of their affairs, and their greedy desire of having the ark of God removed, made them inconsiderate. In Gibeah - Or, on the hill, as 1 Sam. vii, 1.

Played before the Lord — Public joy should always be as before the Lord, with an eye to him, and terminating in him. Otherwise it is no better than public madness, and the source of all manner of wickedness.

Danced — To express his thankfulness to God by his outward carriage, according to the manner of those times. Linen ephod - The usual habit of the priests and Levites, in their sacred ministrations yet sometimes worn by others, as it was by the young child Samuel; and so David, who laid by his royal robes, and put on this robe to declare, that although he was king of Israel, yet he willingly owned himself to be the Lord's minister and servant.
Despised — As one of a base and mean spirit, that knew not how to carry himself with that majesty which became his place.
David had pitched — For Moses tabernacle was still at Gibeon, 1 Chron. xvi, 39; xxi, 29; 2 Chron. i, 3, which David left there, because he designed to build a temple at Jerusalem with all speed.

He blessed — That is, he heartily and solemnly prayed to God for his blessing upon them: which he did both as a prophet, and as their king, to whom by office it belongs, by all means, to seek his people's welfare.

glossa.text: *He gathered together.* ((RAB., ex Euch.)) David, Christ, etc., *as far as* they who, coming down from Judaea, taught the brethren: *Unless you be circumcised after the manner of Moses, you cannot be saved ((Act. XV))*.

*Of him that sitteth.* Above the ark was a tablet which two cherubim covered with their wings, between whom the Lord appeared and spoke.

((RAB., ex Greg.)) In the history of David the king and prophet, by which he is said to have brought up the ark of God, humility is shown approved, pride condemned, and rashness avenged. For David, who did not blush to dance humbly before the ark, soon deserved to receive the promise of the Son of God who should be born of his stock, and his wife, who despised his humility, paid the penalty of perpetual barrenness. The priest also, who rashly touched the ark, purged the guilt of his own daring by an untimely death. Wherein it is to be considered how greatly he offends who approaches the body of the Lord guilty, if that man is punished with death who handled the ark, the figure of the Lord's body, with less veneration than he ought.

((GREG., l. V Moral., cap. 10.)) Often, because they cannot be understood, etc., *as far as* they should not judge the deeds or words of better men as though they were weak.
*With a linen ephod, and David,* etc. ((RAB.)) Not with a pontifical but with a linen garment, for humility's sake, etc., *as far as* he triumphed amid scourges.

*And when he had entered the ark.* ((ID.)) While all were exulting and sounding hymns at the entrance of the heavenly citadel, etc., *as far as* because they who receive the word of God only as far as the ear, without the offspring of good work, await the day of everlasting death.

notes.text: Seas — The whole collection of waters, as well as the sea and the rivers running into it, as that great abyss of waters which is contained in the bowels of the earth.

The hill — Zion or Moriah, the place of God's sanctuary and special presence. Having asserted God's dominion over all mankind, he now proposes an important question, by whom God will be served, and his blessing enjoyed? Stand - To minister before him. Standing is the posture of ministers or servants. Who shall serve God, with God's acceptation. Holy place - In the place which he hath sanctified for his service.

He — Whose actions and conversation are holy and unblameable. Pure heart - Careful to approve itself to God, as well as to men; ordering a man's very thoughts and affections according to God's word. Vanity - Who doth not value or desire the vain things of this life, such as honours, riches, pleasures; but makes God his portion.
The blessing — Grace and glory, and all other good things.
The generation — The true progeny which God regards. Face - His grace and favour, which is often called God's face.

Lift up — He speaks here of the gates and doors of the temple, which by faith and the spirit of prophecy, he beheld as already built, whose doors he calls Everlasting, not so much because they were made of strong and durable materials, as in opposition to those of the tabernacle, which were removed from place to place. These gates he bids lift up their heads, or tops, by allusion to those gates which have a portcullis, which may be let down or taken up. And as the temple was a type of Christ, and of his church, and of heaven itself; so this place may also contain a representation, either of Christ's entrance into his church, or into the hearts of his faithful people, who are here commanded to set open their hearts and souls for his reception: or of his ascension into heaven, where the saints or angels are poetically introduced as preparing the way, and opening the heavenly gates to receive their Lord and king, returning to his royal habitation with triumph and glory. The king - The Messiah, the king of Israel, and of his church, called the King, or Lord of glory, 1 Cor. ii, 8 James ii, 1, both for that glory which is inherent in him, and that which is purchased by him for his members.
The Lord — He is no ordinary person, no other than Jehovah, who hath given so many proofs of his almightiness, who hath subdued all his enemies, and is now returned in triumph.

Lift up — The same verse is repeated again, to awaken the dulness of mankind, who are so hardly brought to a serious preparation for such solemnities; and to signify the great importance of the matter, contained under these expressions.

Of hosts — Under whose command are all the hosts of heaven and earth, angels and men, and all other creatures. David distrest, takes refuge in God, ver. 1-7. Shews the goodness of God to them that fear him, ver. 8-15. Prays for help against his enemies, and for the church, ver. 16-22. A psalm of David.

glossa.text: *A psalm of David.* ((AUG.)) On the first day of the week the world was founded, on the same day man was restored through the resurrection of Christ: ((CASS.)) whence he admonishes us to receive the conqueror with triumph. *The earth is the Lord's.* First he says that the whole world is God's, etc., *as far as* but who shall be in his mountain, save the innocent?

*And upon the ri

* [n: (AUG.)] As rivers glide into the sea, so the covetous glide into the world; and these too the Church overcomes, which, its covetous desires being conquered, is made ready for immortality.
*Who shall ascend?* He determines with what virtues they are endowed in the Church.

*Who shall stand?* ((HIER.)) For many ascend who do not abide. ((ID.)) *The innocent:* toward his neighbour, in hand and in heart, and he who is innocent toward himself, etc., *as far as* they should desire his presence and his knowledge. *Who hath not taken.* ((AUG., HIER.)) That is, who has not reckoned his soul among things that do not abide, but perceiving it immortal shall desire things eternal, and therefore has not sworn deceitfully. *In vain.* ((HIER.)) That is, who has stained it with no dregs of sins after baptism.

*Lift up.* Diapsalmus. Christian religion having been declared, etc., *as far as* which were set there by the prince the devil. *And be ye lifted up.* Against the gates of death. *Ye everlasting gates:* all the grace which, at Christ's coming, was given.
*Who is?* he asks. The Prophet, to convict the perfidy of the Jews, and that by commending him the more he may invite others.

*The Lord strong* is described by his powers as though by his proper name. *Strong,* ((AUG.)) even if ye took him with swords.

*Mighty,* even if ye delivered him to Pilate.

 *Mighty in battle,* lest ye think ye have overcome him in the fight. *The powers.* ((Hier., AUG.)) The ministering powers going before Christ in the ascension cry out to the other heavenly ones, that they may open the way to the Lord as he comes: and these, astonished at the new mystery of one clothed in flesh, ask, who is he?

*Lift up.* ((CASS.)) A doubling, etc., *as far as* who gives all good things to all, or of the heavenly powers, that is, of the angels.

notes.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us — God's blessing us is his bestowing all spiritual and heavenly blessings upon us. Our blessing God is the paying him our solemn and grateful acknowledgments, both on account of his own essential blessedness, and of the blessings which he bestows upon us. He is the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, as man and Mediator: he is his Father, primarily, with respect to his divine nature, as his only begotten Son; and, secondarily, with respect to his human nature, as that is personally united to the divine. With all spiritual blessings in heavenly things - With all manner of spiritual blessings, which are heavenly in their nature, original, and tendency, and shall be completed in heaven: far different from the external privileges of the Jews, and the earthly blessings they expected from the Messiah.
As he hath chosen us — Both Jews and gentiles, whom he foreknew as believing in Christ, 1 Pet. i, 2.

Having predestinated us to the adoption of sons — Having foreordained that all who afterwards believed should enjoy the dignity of being sons of God, and joint-heirs with Christ. According to the good pleasure of his will - According to his free, fixed, unalterable purpose to confer this blessing on all those who should believe in Christ, and those only.
To the praise of the glory of his grace — His glorious, free love without any desert on our part.

By whom we — Who believe. Have - From the moment we believe. Redemption - From the guilt and power of sin. Through his blood - Through what he hath done and suffered for us. According to the riches of his grace - According to the abundant overflowings of his free mercy and favour.
In all wisdom — Manifested by God in the whole scheme of our salvation. And prudence - Which be hath wrought in us, that we may know and do all his acceptable and perfect will.

Having made known to us — By his word and by his Spirit. The mystery of his will - The gracious scheme of salvation by faith, which depends on his own sovereign will alone. This was but darkly discovered under the law; is now totally hid from unbelievers; and has heights and depths which surpass all the knowledge even of true believers.

That in the dispensation of the fulness of the times — In this last administration of God's fullest grace, which took place when the time appointed was fully come. He might gather together into one in Christ - Might recapitulate, re-unite, and place in order again under Christ, their common Head. All things which are in heaven, and on earth - All angels and men, whether living or dead, in the Lord.

Through whom we — Jews. Also have obtained an inheritance - The glorious inheritance of the heavenly Canaan, to which, when believers, we were predestinated according to the purpose of him that worketh all things after the counsel of his own will - The unalterable decree, "He that believeth shall be delivered;" which will is not an arbitrary will, but flowing from the rectitude of his nature, else, what security would there be that it would be his will to keep his word even with the elect?

That we — Jews. Who first believed - Before the gentiles. So did some of them in every place. Here is another branch of the true gospel predestination: he that believes is not only elected to salvation, (if he endures to the end,) but is fore-appointed of God to walk in holiness, to the praise of his glory.

In whom ye — Gentiles. Likewise believed, after ye had heard the gospel - Which God made the means of your salvation; in whom after ye had believed - Probably some time after their first believing. Ye were sealed by that Holy Spirit of promise - Holy both in his nature and in his operations, and promised to all the children of God. The sealing seems to imply,

1. A full impression of the image of God on their souls.

2. A full assurance of receiving all the promises, whether relating to time or eternity.

Who, thus sealing us, is an earnest — Both a pledge and a foretaste of our inheritance. Till the redemption of the purchased possession - Till the church, which he has purchased with his own blood, shall be fully delivered from all sin and sorrow, and advanced to everlasting glory. To the praise of his glory - Of his glorious wisdom, power, and mercy.

glossa.text: *Blessed.* The salutation having been set first, he begins from the giving of thanks, intimating that all things are from God. *He hath blessed.* The word of blessing is indeed one, but according to what befits the person it must be understood in various ways. God is blessed by man, when he is extolled with worthy praises. But man is blessed by God, when God imparts to him the gifts of his grace, not by that man's merits, but by his own mercy.

*Even as he chose,* etc. Let no one, then, suppose that souls are eternal with God, and that they then merited something, according to the error of those who say that before these visible things there were certain holy souls, and that they were therefore then chosen.

*Who predestinated.* A predestination having been set down which pertains to the justice and holiness of the present life, another is here set down pertaining to eternal life, whose effect he noted above.

*Unto the praise of the glory of his grace,* etc. As if he should say: the glory of the graces is the eternal adoption. *In which he hath shown grace.* The effect of the first preordination unto justice. *In the beloved Son.* God the Father loving his only-begotten, the Son lavishes divine things upon those whom he loves and to whom he wills.
*In whom we have,* etc. He shows a twofold grace, because he both redeemed, and did not impute our sins.
*Which hath superabounded.* Thus far concerning those things which [he gave] to the whole human race: now he speaks of those which he gave to the apostles singularly.

*In the dispensation.* That is, in the fullness of the time dispensed by God, that is, in this time of grace, in which the divine providence reasonably dispensed to fulfil the things which in other times were promised or prefigured. For if men were utterly ignorant, not taught beforehand, they would not receive Christ, and unless the proud had first been convicted by the natural and the doctrinal law, they would little esteem the coming of Christ.

 *To restore. ((AUG.))* Now those things are restored which are in the heavens, etc., *as far as* they are renewed from the oldness of corruption.

*All things, which are in the heavens.* That is, the angels; or: *to restore,* that is, to fill up. *Which are in the earth.* That is, men, who had been depraved by sin. *In him.* That is, through Christ.

*In whom we also.* Lest the apostles, in whom grace superabounds, should seem to have deserved better than others, he shows that they were thus called freely, not by merits, even as others also were. *By lot.* Grace is called a lot, because it is not the choice of man, but of the will of God. Whence the Lord's tunic woven from above, which signifies charity, came by lot. *He worketh all things.* Even to will the good, and that we should begin to believe, so that by our example no one may glory in man. For it is true: *You have not chosen me, but I you,* etc. And the praise of the glory of God is when many are gained unto the faith, as the glory of a physician is when he cures many.
*In whom you.* Now he comes to those things which he gave to the Ephesians. *When you had heard. When* here notes the cause, and the time.

notes.text: Matt. xiv, 1; Luke ix, 7.
A prophet, as one of the prophets — Not inferior to one of the ancient prophets.
But Herod hearing thereof — Of their various judgments concerning him, still said, It is John.

And preserved him — Against all the malice and contrivances of Herodias. And when he heard him - Probably sending for him, at times, during his imprisonment, which continued a year and a half. He heard him gladly - Delusive joy! While Herodias lay in his bosom.
A convenient day — Convenient for her purpose. His lords, captains, and principal men of Galilee - The great men of the court, the army, and the province.
To the half of my kingdom — A proverbial expression.
Yet for his oath's sake, and for the sake of his guests — Herod's honour was like the conscience of the chief priests, Matt. xxvii, 6. To shed innocent blood wounded neither one nor the other.

glossa.text: *And the king heard. ((ID.))* Luke ((Luc. IX)): *Herod the tetrarch heard all things that were done,* etc. Whence it is to be understood that either, being confirmed by the words of others, he said it in belief, or that he was still hesitating, etc., *as far as* they chose rather to believe that he had not risen again, but had been carried off by stealth.

*Of Philip his brother. ((BEDA.))* An ancient history relates that Philip was the son of the elder Herod, and the brother of that Herod under whom the Lord suffered, and that he married Herodias the daughter of Aretas, and that afterwards Aretas, quarrels having arisen, took away his own daughter, and joined her in marriage to Herod, the enemy of Philip, to Philip's own grief. Egesippus, however, or Josephus, far otherwise.

*It is not lawful for thee to have,* etc. ((ID.)) He who had come in the spirit and power of Elias reproves Herod and Herodias, as, etc., *as far as* for man is born to labour, and the saints pass through death to rest.

*And he swore. ((BEDA.))* He is not excused from perjury by his oath. For perhaps he swore for this reason, that he might find an occasion of killing. And if she had asked the death of her father or of her mother, Herod assuredly would not have granted it.

*And being made sorrowful,* etc. ((ID.)) Made sorrowful after the accustomed manner of Scripture, not in fact, but in the opinion of many. As Joseph himself also, etc., *as far as* that under the occasion of piety he might become impious.
*His head in a dish. ((ID.))* The head of the law, which is Christ, is cut off from the body, etc., *as far as* but Christ, who is the light of the world, when the days begin to grow.

*And they took. ((ID.))* Josephus relates that John was bound, brought into the castle of Macherus and there beheaded. The Ecclesiastical history relates that it was in Sebaste, a city of Palestine, which was once called Samaria. But in the time of Julian, etc., *as far as* the temple of Serapis being purged of its filth, he laid those same bones there, and consecrated a basilica in honour of Saint John.

echoes.text: Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, from everlasting and to everlasting! Amen and amen.
echoes.note: 'Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ' reproduces the Jewish berakah formula 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,' which closes Book I of the Psalter. Volume is high (verbatim opening 'Blessed be the God'); recurrence across the Psalter (41:13; 72:18; 106:48) and Israel's liturgy makes the form availably and thematically coherent as the native idiom of doxological praise.

echoes.text: Praise be to Yahweh God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds.
echoes.note: The eulogetos opening directly imitates the doxological berakah 'Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel,' another Psalter book-closing blessing. Recurrence with 41:13 and 106:48 establishes the form as a standing liturgical pattern Paul Christologically reworks ('the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ'). Thematic coherence with the eulogetos genre is exact.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God. Yahweh your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth. Yahweh didn’t set his love on you, nor choose you, because you were more in number than any people; for you were the fewest of all peoples: but because Yahweh loves you, and because he desires to keep the oath which he swore to your fathers, Yahweh has brought you out with a mighty hand, […]
echoes.note: 'He chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we would be holy' transposes Israel's election: 'the LORD has chosen you to be a people for his own possession... holy.' Volume is strong (the verb 'chose' + the purpose 'holy'); recurrence in Deuteronomy's election theology and thematic coherence (gratuitous love, not merit) make this the controlling OT subtext for predestination language.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God, and Yahweh has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth.
echoes.note: 'The LORD has chosen you to be a people for his own possession... a holy people' supplies both the election verb and the 'holy/possession' pairing that Ephesians 1:4 and 1:14 develop. Recurrence with Deut 7:6 reinforces a settled Deuteronomic formula; thematic coherence with adoption and inheritance is high.

echoes.text: You shall tell Pharaoh, ‘Thus says Yahweh, Israel is my son, my firstborn,
echoes.note: 'Adoption as children' (huiothesia) presupposes Israel's sonship: 'Israel is my son, my firstborn.' Volume is conceptual rather than verbal, but recurrence (Hos 11:1; Jer 31:9) and thematic coherence with election and inheritance make Israel's adoptive sonship the OT matrix Paul universalizes in Christ.

echoes.text: and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” Abram gave him a tenth of all.
echoes.note: Melchizedek's 'Blessed be God Most High' is the patriarchal prototype of the berakah Paul deploys. Availability and thematic coherence (blessing the God who delivers and gives) support the link, though the volume is lower than the Psalter parallels, since the verbal overlap is only the opening 'Blessed be God.'

echoes.text: “Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘You shall be holy; for I, Yahweh your God, am holy.
echoes.note: 'Holy and without defect before him' draws on the Holiness Code's 'You shall be holy, for I... am holy,' and the sacrificial demand that an offering be 'without blemish' (Lev 1:3; 22:21). Thematic coherence (Israel/offering presented blameless to God) is strong; the volume is diffuse because two strands of Levitical holiness merge.

echoes.text: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.
echoes.note: 'When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son' ties adoption to redemptive love and election, the same cluster Ephesians 1:4-6 fuses ('in love... adoption'). Recurrence with Exod 4:22 strengthens the sonship motif; the volume is thematic, marked medium because Ephesians does not cite the wording.

echoes.text: He said, “Now take your son, your only son, whom you love, even Isaac, and go into the land of Moriah. Offer him there for a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you of.”
echoes.note: 'The Beloved' (en to egapemeno) evokes Isaac, 'your son, your only son, whom you love,' the beloved offered son — apt for a passage moving toward 'redemption through his blood.' Thematic coherence (beloved son, sacrifice) is good; the volume is moderate because 'Beloved' also draws on Psalm 2 and Isaiah 5 traditions.

echoes.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
echoes.note: The royal decree 'You are my son; today I have begotten you,' read messianically in Second-Temple Judaism, undergirds the 'Beloved' Son in whom believers are adopted as sons. Recurrence of Psalm 2 in NT sonship texts and thematic coherence (divine sonship grounding adoption) support a medium-confidence echo.

echoes.text: Let me sing for my well beloved a song of my beloved about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a very fruitful hill.
echoes.note: Isaiah's Song 'for my beloved' (to egapemeno LXX) is one of the LXX loci where ho egapemenos functions almost titularly, a possible reservoir for Ephesians' 'in the Beloved.' Availability is genuine, but volume and thematic coherence are weak here, so the echo is marked low and contested.

echoes.text: Therefore tell the children of Israel, ‘I am Yahweh, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments:
echoes.note: 'Redemption' (apolytrosis) maps onto the exodus paradigm: 'I will redeem you with an outstretched arm.' Volume is conceptual but strong; recurrence of redemption-from-Egypt language across the OT and thematic coherence with deliverance and possession (cf. 1:14) make the exodus the governing pattern for 'redemption through his blood.'

echoes.text: Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, “Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which Yahweh has made with you concerning all these words.”
echoes.note: 'Redemption through his blood' coupled with covenant draws on the blood of the covenant Moses dashed on the people, 'the blood of the covenant the LORD has made.' Thematic coherence (blood ratifying covenant deliverance) is solid; volume is moderate because Ephesians names redemption and forgiveness rather than covenant explicitly.

echoes.text: But now thus says Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
echoes.note: 'I have redeemed you; I have called you by name; you are mine' fuses redemption, calling, and possession exactly as Ephesians 1:7,14 do. Isaiah's new-exodus redemption is availably and thematically coherent with Paul's apolytrosis; medium because the link is motivic, not verbal.

echoes.text: Israel, hope in Yahweh, for with Yahweh there is loving kindness. With him is abundant redemption. He will redeem Israel from all their sins.
echoes.note: 'With the LORD... is plentiful redemption. He will redeem Israel from all his iniquities' joins redemption to forgiveness of sins, the precise pairing of Ephesians 1:7 ('redemption... the forgiveness of our trespasses'). Thematic coherence is high; volume moderate, so medium confidence.

echoes.text: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these: as for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what shall happen.
echoes.note: 'Making known to us the mystery of his will' draws on Daniel's God 'who reveals mysteries' and 'made known... what will be.' Volume is strong (mysterion + the verb 'make known' is distinctively Danielic in the LXX); recurrence (Dan 2:19,30,47) and thematic coherence (eschatological disclosure of God's hidden purpose) make this the primary subtext for Ephesians' mystery language.

echoes.text: The king answered to Daniel, and said, Of a truth your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.
echoes.note: 'Your God is... a revealer of mysteries, since you could reveal this mystery' reinforces the Danielic provenance of 'the mystery of his will' made known. Recurrence within Daniel 2 strengthens the allusion; medium because it overlaps with 2:28-29 rather than adding distinct wording.

echoes.text: declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that are not yet done; saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure;
echoes.note: 'Him who works all things after the counsel of his will' echoes Isaiah's God 'declaring the end from the beginning... my counsel shall stand, and I will accomplish all my purpose.' Thematic coherence (sovereign counsel/purpose executed in history) is strong; volume is moderate, hence a medium echo.

echoes.text: All the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing; and he does according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth; and no one can stay his hand, or ask him, What are you doing?
echoes.note: 'Works all things after the counsel of his will' resonates with Daniel's confession that God 'does according to his will... none can stay his hand.' Availability and thematic coherence (universal divine sovereignty) support a faint echo; volume is low, so it is marked contested.

echoes.text: The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat; The calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf together; and a little child will lead them. The cow and the bear will graze. Their young ones will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox. The nursing child will play near a cobra’s hole, and the weaned child will put his hand on the viper’s den. They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain; for […]
echoes.note: 'To sum up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens and the things on the earth' may resonate with Isaiah's eschatological reconciliation of all creation under the Messianic shoot. Thematic coherence (cosmic harmony restored under the Anointed) is plausible but the volume is low; marked contested.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: 'Sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise' draws on the eschatological promise 'I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh.' The Spirit as 'of promise' coheres with Joel's prophetic gift inaugurating the last days; recurrence in Second-Temple expectation and thematic coherence (Spirit marking the eschatological people) support a high-confidence allusion.

echoes.text: I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: 'I will put my Spirit within you' is the new-covenant promise behind the indwelling 'Spirit of promise.' Thematic coherence (Spirit given to a redeemed possession, cleansed and made holy) matches Ephesians' election/holiness frame; recurrence with Ezek 37:14 and 39:29 strengthens the link.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God, and Yahweh has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth.
echoes.note: 'The redemption of God's own possession' reproduces Deuteronomy's 'a people for his own possession (peripoiesis/segullah).' Volume is strong on the possession motif; recurrence (Deut 7:6; 26:18; Exod 19:5) and thematic coherence (redeemed people belonging to God) make this a controlling subtext for 1:14.

echoes.text: Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my voice, and keep my covenant, then you shall be my own possession from among all peoples; for all the earth is mine;
echoes.note: 'You shall be my own possession among all peoples' (segullah / LXX laos periousios) underlies 'the redemption of God's own possession.' Recurrence with Deut 7:6 and 14:2 and thematic coherence (covenant possession claimed and redeemed) reinforce the allusion; the volume on the possession concept is high.

echoes.text: In that day, says Yahweh of Armies, will I take you, Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel,’ says Yahweh, ‘and will make you as a signet, for I have chosen you,’ says Yahweh of Armies.”
echoes.note: 'You were sealed' (esphragisthete) evokes Haggai's 'I will make you like a signet ring (sphragis), for I have chosen you,' which joins the seal image to divine election — the very pairing of Ephesians 1:4,13. Thematic coherence is strong; medium because the seal in Ephesians is the Spirit, not the person.

echoes.text: For he said, “Surely, they are my people, children who will not deal falsely:” so he was their Savior. In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bore them, and carried them all the days of old.
echoes.note: 'They are my people... so he became their Savior... he redeemed them' joins God's people, Spirit, and redemption — the cluster of Ephesians 1:13-14. Thematic coherence is decent but the volume is faint, so this is a low, contested echo.

echoes.text: They shall be mine,” says Yahweh of Armies, “my own possession in the day that I make, and I will spare them, as a man spares his own son who serves him.
echoes.note: 'They shall be mine, says the LORD of hosts, my own possession (segullah)' on the day God acts could reinforce 'the redemption of God's own possession' with an eschatological cast. Recurrence of the segullah term supports availability; volume is low, hence contested.

echoes.text: Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword. Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, “So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I don’t make your life as the life of one of them by tomorrow about this time!”
echoes.note: Jezebel, the powerful queen, vows to kill the prophet Elijah, who is identified in this very passage (v. 15) with the figure expected to return. Herodias' relentless desire to kill John, the Elijah-figure, replays the Jezebel-versus-prophet conflict. Strong thematic coherence and recurrence, reinforced by Mark's explicit Elijah identification.

echoes.text: After these things, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard, which was in Jezreel, hard by the palace of Ahab king of Samaria. Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, “Give me your vineyard, that I may have it for a garden of herbs, because it is near to my house; and I will give you for it a better vineyard than it. Or, if it seems good to you, I will give you its worth in money.” Naboth said to Ahab, “May Yahweh forbid me, that I should give the inheritance of my […]
echoes.note: Jezebel manipulates a royal feast and oath/legal machinery to bring about Naboth's death while the weak king Ahab acquiesces. Herodias engineers John's execution through her daughter at a banquet while a reluctant Herod yields, a deliberate Ahab-Jezebel-Naboth typology. The wicked-queen-orchestrates-judicial-murder pattern is tightly coherent.

echoes.text: Then the king asked her, “What would you like, queen Esther? What is your request? It shall be given you even to the half of the kingdom.”
echoes.note: Ahasuerus, at a banquet, offers Esther her request 'up to half of my kingdom,' the exact royal-oath formula Herod swears to the dancing girl (also Esther 5:6; 7:2). The verbal correspondence is precise and distinctive, making this a near-quotation of the Persian-court motif. High volume and recurrence within Esther.

echoes.text: “‘You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife. It is your brother’s nakedness.
echoes.note: John's charge, 'It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife,' directly invokes the Levitical prohibition against uncovering the nakedness of a brother's wife. The legal ground of John's rebuke is this statute (cf. Lev 20:21). The verbal and legal correspondence is explicit.

echoes.text: “‘If a man takes his brother’s wife, it is an impurity. He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness. They shall be childless.
echoes.note: This statute declares it 'impurity' for a man to take his brother's wife, the precise offense John names against Herod for marrying Herodias. Together with Lev 18:16 it furnishes the explicit legal basis of the prophet's condemnation. Direct invocation of Torah.

echoes.text: for it was so, when Jezebel cut off the prophets of Yahweh, that Obadiah took one hundred prophets, and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water.)
echoes.note: Jezebel cuts off (kills) the prophets of Yahweh while Obadiah hides them, establishing the queen-as-prophet-killer. John's beheading at the queen's instigation reprises this. The Elijah-cycle background that Mark foregrounds strengthens the echo.

echoes.text: The king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son. Say, ‘Thus says the king, “Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I come in peace.”’”
echoes.note: King Ahab imprisons the prophet Micaiah for speaking an unwelcome word. Herod's binding John in prison for his unwelcome rebuke replays the king-imprisons-truthful-prophet motif. Contested, thematic coherence within the Kings prophetic cycle.

echoes.text: Then took they Jeremiah, and cast him into the dungeon of Malchijah the king’s son, that was in the court of the guard: and they let down Jeremiah with cords. In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire. Now when Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, a eunuch, who was in the king’s house, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the dungeon (the king then sitting in the gate of Benjamin), Ebedmelech went out of the king’s house, and spoke to […]
echoes.note: Jeremiah is imprisoned by officials while a vacillating king Zedekiah privately respects yet fails to protect him. Herod's fearing and gladly hearing John yet failing to save him mirrors the weak-king-and-imprisoned-prophet dynamic. Faint and contested.

echoes.text: The fear of man proves to be a snare, but whoever puts his trust in Yahweh is kept safe.
echoes.note: The fear of human opinion becomes a snare. Herod's capitulation 'for the sake of his oaths and of his dinner guests' illustrates this proverbial snare of social fear. Wisdom-thematic resonance only; contested.

echoes.text: Jephthah vowed a vow to Yahweh, and said, “If you will indeed deliver the children of Ammon into my hand, then it shall be, that whatever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, it shall be Yahweh’s, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering.” So Jephthah passed over to the children of Ammon to fight against them; and Yahweh delivered them into his hand. He struck them from Aroer until you come […]
echoes.note: Jephthah's rash vow forces him to a deadly act he regrets, the king-bound-by-his-oath tragedy. Herod, 'exceedingly sorry' yet bound 'for the sake of his oaths,' replays this rash-vow type. Contested, thematic and structural parallel without verbal link.

echoes.text: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cup bearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants. He restored the chief cup bearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand; but he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.
echoes.note: Pharaoh's birthday feast becomes the occasion of an execution, the only other clear OT royal birthday banquet ending in death. Herod's birthday supper culminating in beheading faintly recalls this. Low confidence, contested resonance.

notes.text: By a plumb-line — Strongly and beautifully built.
Set a plumb-line — I will exactly measure the whole ten tribes. Pass by them - I will no more forbear, but will pull down all that is faulty.
The high places — The temples on high mountains built to idols. Of Isaac - The seed of Isaac.
In the midst — Openly, and publickly, endeavouring to stir up Israel to sedition or rebellion. The land - The people cannot bear all his harsh predictions.
Jeroboam shall die — He nowhere said so, but spake of his house distinguished from his person, as ver. 9.
The king's court — To which therefore thou oughtest to shew more respect, and not thus to affront the king in his own house.

No prophet — Not originally, or by study, or by any human designation. An herdman - By breeding and occupation I was and still am, an herdman. Sycamore fruit - This fruit was good food for man, or cattle.

Will hear — Diligently observe. Will speak - What answer God will give to my prayers. Peace - He will give an answer of peace. Saints - Not to all that are called God's people, but only to those who are truly such.

His salvation — That compleat salvation for which all the Israel of God wait; even the redemption by the Messiah; of which not only Christian, but even Jewish writers understand this place; and to which the following passages properly belong. And the psalmist might well say this salvation was nigh, because the seventy weeks determined by Daniel were begun. Glory - The glorious presence of God, and the God of glory himself, even Christ, who is the brightness of his father's glory.

Kissed — That great work of redemption by Christ, shall clearly manifest God's mercy in redeeming his people Israel, and in the conversion of the Gentiles; his truth in fulfilling that great promise of sending his son, his righteousness in punishing sin, on his son, and in conferring righteousness upon guilty and lost creatures; and his peace or reconciliation to sinners, and that peace of conscience which attends upon it.
Truth — Truth among men. Righteousness - And God's justice shall be satisfied: he shall look down upon sinful men with a smiling countenance.

Before him — As his harbinger. He shall fulfil all righteousness, he shall satisfy the righteousness of God, and shall advance righteousness and holiness among men. Set us - Shall cause us to walk in those righteous ways wherein he walketh. David prays for the favour and blessing of God, ver. 1-6. Expresses confidence in him, by praise mingled with prayer, ver. 7-17. A prayer of David.

glossa.text: *I will hear what the Lord speaketh in me.* ((CASS.)) Whence he knows, and by whom it is done, and what he himself bestows in coming. *Peace.* ((AUG.)) Christ. Peace toward God and toward the neighbour, and through Christ.
*Near them that fear him.* ((ID.)) Everywhere demons were worshipped, etc., *as far as* immortal in our body now mortal.
*Mercy,* etc. ((ID.)) After he had said, etc., *as far as how truth is sprung out of the earth ((Luc. VIII))*.
*Truth is sprung out of the earth.* ((ID.)) Confession from man, that he may accuse himself, etc., *as far as* the justification of him that confesses is given.

*Justice shall go before him.* ((ID.)) The first justice of man is, etc., *as far as* and visiting he shall set his steps in the way. *Shall walk.* It shall increase, or shall run before, preparing the way for him; and the Lord shall set his steps in the way made ready.

notes.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us — God's blessing us is his bestowing all spiritual and heavenly blessings upon us. Our blessing God is the paying him our solemn and grateful acknowledgments, both on account of his own essential blessedness, and of the blessings which he bestows upon us. He is the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, as man and Mediator: he is his Father, primarily, with respect to his divine nature, as his only begotten Son; and, secondarily, with respect to his human nature, as that is personally united to the divine. With all spiritual blessings in heavenly things - With all manner of spiritual blessings, which are heavenly in their nature, original, and tendency, and shall be completed in heaven: far different from the external privileges of the Jews, and the earthly blessings they expected from the Messiah.
As he hath chosen us — Both Jews and gentiles, whom he foreknew as believing in Christ, 1 Pet. i, 2.

Having predestinated us to the adoption of sons — Having foreordained that all who afterwards believed should enjoy the dignity of being sons of God, and joint-heirs with Christ. According to the good pleasure of his will - According to his free, fixed, unalterable purpose to confer this blessing on all those who should believe in Christ, and those only.
To the praise of the glory of his grace — His glorious, free love without any desert on our part.

By whom we — Who believe. Have - From the moment we believe. Redemption - From the guilt and power of sin. Through his blood - Through what he hath done and suffered for us. According to the riches of his grace - According to the abundant overflowings of his free mercy and favour.
In all wisdom — Manifested by God in the whole scheme of our salvation. And prudence - Which be hath wrought in us, that we may know and do all his acceptable and perfect will.

Having made known to us — By his word and by his Spirit. The mystery of his will - The gracious scheme of salvation by faith, which depends on his own sovereign will alone. This was but darkly discovered under the law; is now totally hid from unbelievers; and has heights and depths which surpass all the knowledge even of true believers.

That in the dispensation of the fulness of the times — In this last administration of God's fullest grace, which took place when the time appointed was fully come. He might gather together into one in Christ - Might recapitulate, re-unite, and place in order again under Christ, their common Head. All things which are in heaven, and on earth - All angels and men, whether living or dead, in the Lord.

Through whom we — Jews. Also have obtained an inheritance - The glorious inheritance of the heavenly Canaan, to which, when believers, we were predestinated according to the purpose of him that worketh all things after the counsel of his own will - The unalterable decree, "He that believeth shall be delivered;" which will is not an arbitrary will, but flowing from the rectitude of his nature, else, what security would there be that it would be his will to keep his word even with the elect?

That we — Jews. Who first believed - Before the gentiles. So did some of them in every place. Here is another branch of the true gospel predestination: he that believes is not only elected to salvation, (if he endures to the end,) but is fore-appointed of God to walk in holiness, to the praise of his glory.

In whom ye — Gentiles. Likewise believed, after ye had heard the gospel - Which God made the means of your salvation; in whom after ye had believed - Probably some time after their first believing. Ye were sealed by that Holy Spirit of promise - Holy both in his nature and in his operations, and promised to all the children of God. The sealing seems to imply,

1. A full impression of the image of God on their souls.

2. A full assurance of receiving all the promises, whether relating to time or eternity.

Who, thus sealing us, is an earnest — Both a pledge and a foretaste of our inheritance. Till the redemption of the purchased possession - Till the church, which he has purchased with his own blood, shall be fully delivered from all sin and sorrow, and advanced to everlasting glory. To the praise of his glory - Of his glorious wisdom, power, and mercy.

glossa.text: *Blessed.* The salutation having been set first, he begins from the giving of thanks, intimating that all things are from God. *He hath blessed.* The word of blessing is indeed one, but according to what befits the person it must be understood in various ways. God is blessed by man, when he is extolled with worthy praises. But man is blessed by God, when God imparts to him the gifts of his grace, not by that man's merits, but by his own mercy.

*Even as he chose,* etc. Let no one, then, suppose that souls are eternal with God, and that they then merited something, according to the error of those who say that before these visible things there were certain holy souls, and that they were therefore then chosen.

*Who predestinated.* A predestination having been set down which pertains to the justice and holiness of the present life, another is here set down pertaining to eternal life, whose effect he noted above.

*Unto the praise of the glory of his grace,* etc. As if he should say: the glory of the graces is the eternal adoption. *In which he hath shown grace.* The effect of the first preordination unto justice. *In the beloved Son.* God the Father loving his only-begotten, the Son lavishes divine things upon those whom he loves and to whom he wills.
*In whom we have,* etc. He shows a twofold grace, because he both redeemed, and did not impute our sins.
*Which hath superabounded.* Thus far concerning those things which [he gave] to the whole human race: now he speaks of those which he gave to the apostles singularly.

*In the dispensation.* That is, in the fullness of the time dispensed by God, that is, in this time of grace, in which the divine providence reasonably dispensed to fulfil the things which in other times were promised or prefigured. For if men were utterly ignorant, not taught beforehand, they would not receive Christ, and unless the proud had first been convicted by the natural and the doctrinal law, they would little esteem the coming of Christ.

 *To restore. ((AUG.))* Now those things are restored which are in the heavens, etc., *as far as* they are renewed from the oldness of corruption.

*All things, which are in the heavens.* That is, the angels; or: *to restore,* that is, to fill up. *Which are in the earth.* That is, men, who had been depraved by sin. *In him.* That is, through Christ.

*In whom we also.* Lest the apostles, in whom grace superabounds, should seem to have deserved better than others, he shows that they were thus called freely, not by merits, even as others also were. *By lot.* Grace is called a lot, because it is not the choice of man, but of the will of God. Whence the Lord's tunic woven from above, which signifies charity, came by lot. *He worketh all things.* Even to will the good, and that we should begin to believe, so that by our example no one may glory in man. For it is true: *You have not chosen me, but I you,* etc. And the praise of the glory of God is when many are gained unto the faith, as the glory of a physician is when he cures many.
*In whom you.* Now he comes to those things which he gave to the Ephesians. *When you had heard. When* here notes the cause, and the time.

notes.text: Matt. xiv, 1; Luke ix, 7.
A prophet, as one of the prophets — Not inferior to one of the ancient prophets.
But Herod hearing thereof — Of their various judgments concerning him, still said, It is John.

And preserved him — Against all the malice and contrivances of Herodias. And when he heard him - Probably sending for him, at times, during his imprisonment, which continued a year and a half. He heard him gladly - Delusive joy! While Herodias lay in his bosom.
A convenient day — Convenient for her purpose. His lords, captains, and principal men of Galilee - The great men of the court, the army, and the province.
To the half of my kingdom — A proverbial expression.
Yet for his oath's sake, and for the sake of his guests — Herod's honour was like the conscience of the chief priests, Matt. xxvii, 6. To shed innocent blood wounded neither one nor the other.

glossa.text: *And the king heard. ((ID.))* Luke ((Luc. IX)): *Herod the tetrarch heard all things that were done,* etc. Whence it is to be understood that either, being confirmed by the words of others, he said it in belief, or that he was still hesitating, etc., *as far as* they chose rather to believe that he had not risen again, but had been carried off by stealth.

*Of Philip his brother. ((BEDA.))* An ancient history relates that Philip was the son of the elder Herod, and the brother of that Herod under whom the Lord suffered, and that he married Herodias the daughter of Aretas, and that afterwards Aretas, quarrels having arisen, took away his own daughter, and joined her in marriage to Herod, the enemy of Philip, to Philip's own grief. Egesippus, however, or Josephus, far otherwise.

*It is not lawful for thee to have,* etc. ((ID.)) He who had come in the spirit and power of Elias reproves Herod and Herodias, as, etc., *as far as* for man is born to labour, and the saints pass through death to rest.

*And he swore. ((BEDA.))* He is not excused from perjury by his oath. For perhaps he swore for this reason, that he might find an occasion of killing. And if she had asked the death of her father or of her mother, Herod assuredly would not have granted it.

*And being made sorrowful,* etc. ((ID.)) Made sorrowful after the accustomed manner of Scripture, not in fact, but in the opinion of many. As Joseph himself also, etc., *as far as* that under the occasion of piety he might become impious.
*His head in a dish. ((ID.))* The head of the law, which is Christ, is cut off from the body, etc., *as far as* but Christ, who is the light of the world, when the days begin to grow.

*And they took. ((ID.))* Josephus relates that John was bound, brought into the castle of Macherus and there beheaded. The Ecclesiastical history relates that it was in Sebaste, a city of Palestine, which was once called Samaria. But in the time of Julian, etc., *as far as* the temple of Serapis being purged of its filth, he laid those same bones there, and consecrated a basilica in honour of Saint John.

echoes.text: Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, from everlasting and to everlasting! Amen and amen.
echoes.note: 'Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ' reproduces the Jewish berakah formula 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,' which closes Book I of the Psalter. Volume is high (verbatim opening 'Blessed be the God'); recurrence across the Psalter (41:13; 72:18; 106:48) and Israel's liturgy makes the form availably and thematically coherent as the native idiom of doxological praise.

echoes.text: Praise be to Yahweh God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds.
echoes.note: The eulogetos opening directly imitates the doxological berakah 'Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel,' another Psalter book-closing blessing. Recurrence with 41:13 and 106:48 establishes the form as a standing liturgical pattern Paul Christologically reworks ('the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ'). Thematic coherence with the eulogetos genre is exact.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God. Yahweh your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth. Yahweh didn’t set his love on you, nor choose you, because you were more in number than any people; for you were the fewest of all peoples: but because Yahweh loves you, and because he desires to keep the oath which he swore to your fathers, Yahweh has brought you out with a mighty hand, […]
echoes.note: 'He chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we would be holy' transposes Israel's election: 'the LORD has chosen you to be a people for his own possession... holy.' Volume is strong (the verb 'chose' + the purpose 'holy'); recurrence in Deuteronomy's election theology and thematic coherence (gratuitous love, not merit) make this the controlling OT subtext for predestination language.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God, and Yahweh has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth.
echoes.note: 'The LORD has chosen you to be a people for his own possession... a holy people' supplies both the election verb and the 'holy/possession' pairing that Ephesians 1:4 and 1:14 develop. Recurrence with Deut 7:6 reinforces a settled Deuteronomic formula; thematic coherence with adoption and inheritance is high.

echoes.text: You shall tell Pharaoh, ‘Thus says Yahweh, Israel is my son, my firstborn,
echoes.note: 'Adoption as children' (huiothesia) presupposes Israel's sonship: 'Israel is my son, my firstborn.' Volume is conceptual rather than verbal, but recurrence (Hos 11:1; Jer 31:9) and thematic coherence with election and inheritance make Israel's adoptive sonship the OT matrix Paul universalizes in Christ.

echoes.text: and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” Abram gave him a tenth of all.
echoes.note: Melchizedek's 'Blessed be God Most High' is the patriarchal prototype of the berakah Paul deploys. Availability and thematic coherence (blessing the God who delivers and gives) support the link, though the volume is lower than the Psalter parallels, since the verbal overlap is only the opening 'Blessed be God.'

echoes.text: “Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘You shall be holy; for I, Yahweh your God, am holy.
echoes.note: 'Holy and without defect before him' draws on the Holiness Code's 'You shall be holy, for I... am holy,' and the sacrificial demand that an offering be 'without blemish' (Lev 1:3; 22:21). Thematic coherence (Israel/offering presented blameless to God) is strong; the volume is diffuse because two strands of Levitical holiness merge.

echoes.text: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.
echoes.note: 'When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son' ties adoption to redemptive love and election, the same cluster Ephesians 1:4-6 fuses ('in love... adoption'). Recurrence with Exod 4:22 strengthens the sonship motif; the volume is thematic, marked medium because Ephesians does not cite the wording.

echoes.text: He said, “Now take your son, your only son, whom you love, even Isaac, and go into the land of Moriah. Offer him there for a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you of.”
echoes.note: 'The Beloved' (en to egapemeno) evokes Isaac, 'your son, your only son, whom you love,' the beloved offered son — apt for a passage moving toward 'redemption through his blood.' Thematic coherence (beloved son, sacrifice) is good; the volume is moderate because 'Beloved' also draws on Psalm 2 and Isaiah 5 traditions.

echoes.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
echoes.note: The royal decree 'You are my son; today I have begotten you,' read messianically in Second-Temple Judaism, undergirds the 'Beloved' Son in whom believers are adopted as sons. Recurrence of Psalm 2 in NT sonship texts and thematic coherence (divine sonship grounding adoption) support a medium-confidence echo.

echoes.text: Let me sing for my well beloved a song of my beloved about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a very fruitful hill.
echoes.note: Isaiah's Song 'for my beloved' (to egapemeno LXX) is one of the LXX loci where ho egapemenos functions almost titularly, a possible reservoir for Ephesians' 'in the Beloved.' Availability is genuine, but volume and thematic coherence are weak here, so the echo is marked low and contested.

echoes.text: Therefore tell the children of Israel, ‘I am Yahweh, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments:
echoes.note: 'Redemption' (apolytrosis) maps onto the exodus paradigm: 'I will redeem you with an outstretched arm.' Volume is conceptual but strong; recurrence of redemption-from-Egypt language across the OT and thematic coherence with deliverance and possession (cf. 1:14) make the exodus the governing pattern for 'redemption through his blood.'

echoes.text: Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, “Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which Yahweh has made with you concerning all these words.”
echoes.note: 'Redemption through his blood' coupled with covenant draws on the blood of the covenant Moses dashed on the people, 'the blood of the covenant the LORD has made.' Thematic coherence (blood ratifying covenant deliverance) is solid; volume is moderate because Ephesians names redemption and forgiveness rather than covenant explicitly.

echoes.text: But now thus says Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
echoes.note: 'I have redeemed you; I have called you by name; you are mine' fuses redemption, calling, and possession exactly as Ephesians 1:7,14 do. Isaiah's new-exodus redemption is availably and thematically coherent with Paul's apolytrosis; medium because the link is motivic, not verbal.

echoes.text: Israel, hope in Yahweh, for with Yahweh there is loving kindness. With him is abundant redemption. He will redeem Israel from all their sins.
echoes.note: 'With the LORD... is plentiful redemption. He will redeem Israel from all his iniquities' joins redemption to forgiveness of sins, the precise pairing of Ephesians 1:7 ('redemption... the forgiveness of our trespasses'). Thematic coherence is high; volume moderate, so medium confidence.

echoes.text: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these: as for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what shall happen.
echoes.note: 'Making known to us the mystery of his will' draws on Daniel's God 'who reveals mysteries' and 'made known... what will be.' Volume is strong (mysterion + the verb 'make known' is distinctively Danielic in the LXX); recurrence (Dan 2:19,30,47) and thematic coherence (eschatological disclosure of God's hidden purpose) make this the primary subtext for Ephesians' mystery language.

echoes.text: The king answered to Daniel, and said, Of a truth your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.
echoes.note: 'Your God is... a revealer of mysteries, since you could reveal this mystery' reinforces the Danielic provenance of 'the mystery of his will' made known. Recurrence within Daniel 2 strengthens the allusion; medium because it overlaps with 2:28-29 rather than adding distinct wording.

echoes.text: declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that are not yet done; saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure;
echoes.note: 'Him who works all things after the counsel of his will' echoes Isaiah's God 'declaring the end from the beginning... my counsel shall stand, and I will accomplish all my purpose.' Thematic coherence (sovereign counsel/purpose executed in history) is strong; volume is moderate, hence a medium echo.

echoes.text: All the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing; and he does according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth; and no one can stay his hand, or ask him, What are you doing?
echoes.note: 'Works all things after the counsel of his will' resonates with Daniel's confession that God 'does according to his will... none can stay his hand.' Availability and thematic coherence (universal divine sovereignty) support a faint echo; volume is low, so it is marked contested.

echoes.text: The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat; The calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf together; and a little child will lead them. The cow and the bear will graze. Their young ones will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox. The nursing child will play near a cobra’s hole, and the weaned child will put his hand on the viper’s den. They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain; for […]
echoes.note: 'To sum up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens and the things on the earth' may resonate with Isaiah's eschatological reconciliation of all creation under the Messianic shoot. Thematic coherence (cosmic harmony restored under the Anointed) is plausible but the volume is low; marked contested.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: 'Sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise' draws on the eschatological promise 'I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh.' The Spirit as 'of promise' coheres with Joel's prophetic gift inaugurating the last days; recurrence in Second-Temple expectation and thematic coherence (Spirit marking the eschatological people) support a high-confidence allusion.

echoes.text: I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: 'I will put my Spirit within you' is the new-covenant promise behind the indwelling 'Spirit of promise.' Thematic coherence (Spirit given to a redeemed possession, cleansed and made holy) matches Ephesians' election/holiness frame; recurrence with Ezek 37:14 and 39:29 strengthens the link.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God, and Yahweh has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth.
echoes.note: 'The redemption of God's own possession' reproduces Deuteronomy's 'a people for his own possession (peripoiesis/segullah).' Volume is strong on the possession motif; recurrence (Deut 7:6; 26:18; Exod 19:5) and thematic coherence (redeemed people belonging to God) make this a controlling subtext for 1:14.

echoes.text: Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my voice, and keep my covenant, then you shall be my own possession from among all peoples; for all the earth is mine;
echoes.note: 'You shall be my own possession among all peoples' (segullah / LXX laos periousios) underlies 'the redemption of God's own possession.' Recurrence with Deut 7:6 and 14:2 and thematic coherence (covenant possession claimed and redeemed) reinforce the allusion; the volume on the possession concept is high.

echoes.text: In that day, says Yahweh of Armies, will I take you, Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel,’ says Yahweh, ‘and will make you as a signet, for I have chosen you,’ says Yahweh of Armies.”
echoes.note: 'You were sealed' (esphragisthete) evokes Haggai's 'I will make you like a signet ring (sphragis), for I have chosen you,' which joins the seal image to divine election — the very pairing of Ephesians 1:4,13. Thematic coherence is strong; medium because the seal in Ephesians is the Spirit, not the person.

echoes.text: For he said, “Surely, they are my people, children who will not deal falsely:” so he was their Savior. In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bore them, and carried them all the days of old.
echoes.note: 'They are my people... so he became their Savior... he redeemed them' joins God's people, Spirit, and redemption — the cluster of Ephesians 1:13-14. Thematic coherence is decent but the volume is faint, so this is a low, contested echo.

echoes.text: They shall be mine,” says Yahweh of Armies, “my own possession in the day that I make, and I will spare them, as a man spares his own son who serves him.
echoes.note: 'They shall be mine, says the LORD of hosts, my own possession (segullah)' on the day God acts could reinforce 'the redemption of God's own possession' with an eschatological cast. Recurrence of the segullah term supports availability; volume is low, hence contested.

echoes.text: Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword. Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, “So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I don’t make your life as the life of one of them by tomorrow about this time!”
echoes.note: Jezebel, the powerful queen, vows to kill the prophet Elijah, who is identified in this very passage (v. 15) with the figure expected to return. Herodias' relentless desire to kill John, the Elijah-figure, replays the Jezebel-versus-prophet conflict. Strong thematic coherence and recurrence, reinforced by Mark's explicit Elijah identification.

echoes.text: After these things, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard, which was in Jezreel, hard by the palace of Ahab king of Samaria. Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, “Give me your vineyard, that I may have it for a garden of herbs, because it is near to my house; and I will give you for it a better vineyard than it. Or, if it seems good to you, I will give you its worth in money.” Naboth said to Ahab, “May Yahweh forbid me, that I should give the inheritance of my […]
echoes.note: Jezebel manipulates a royal feast and oath/legal machinery to bring about Naboth's death while the weak king Ahab acquiesces. Herodias engineers John's execution through her daughter at a banquet while a reluctant Herod yields, a deliberate Ahab-Jezebel-Naboth typology. The wicked-queen-orchestrates-judicial-murder pattern is tightly coherent.

echoes.text: Then the king asked her, “What would you like, queen Esther? What is your request? It shall be given you even to the half of the kingdom.”
echoes.note: Ahasuerus, at a banquet, offers Esther her request 'up to half of my kingdom,' the exact royal-oath formula Herod swears to the dancing girl (also Esther 5:6; 7:2). The verbal correspondence is precise and distinctive, making this a near-quotation of the Persian-court motif. High volume and recurrence within Esther.

echoes.text: “‘You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife. It is your brother’s nakedness.
echoes.note: John's charge, 'It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife,' directly invokes the Levitical prohibition against uncovering the nakedness of a brother's wife. The legal ground of John's rebuke is this statute (cf. Lev 20:21). The verbal and legal correspondence is explicit.

echoes.text: “‘If a man takes his brother’s wife, it is an impurity. He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness. They shall be childless.
echoes.note: This statute declares it 'impurity' for a man to take his brother's wife, the precise offense John names against Herod for marrying Herodias. Together with Lev 18:16 it furnishes the explicit legal basis of the prophet's condemnation. Direct invocation of Torah.

echoes.text: for it was so, when Jezebel cut off the prophets of Yahweh, that Obadiah took one hundred prophets, and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water.)
echoes.note: Jezebel cuts off (kills) the prophets of Yahweh while Obadiah hides them, establishing the queen-as-prophet-killer. John's beheading at the queen's instigation reprises this. The Elijah-cycle background that Mark foregrounds strengthens the echo.

echoes.text: The king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son. Say, ‘Thus says the king, “Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I come in peace.”’”
echoes.note: King Ahab imprisons the prophet Micaiah for speaking an unwelcome word. Herod's binding John in prison for his unwelcome rebuke replays the king-imprisons-truthful-prophet motif. Contested, thematic coherence within the Kings prophetic cycle.

echoes.text: Then took they Jeremiah, and cast him into the dungeon of Malchijah the king’s son, that was in the court of the guard: and they let down Jeremiah with cords. In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire. Now when Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, a eunuch, who was in the king’s house, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the dungeon (the king then sitting in the gate of Benjamin), Ebedmelech went out of the king’s house, and spoke to […]
echoes.note: Jeremiah is imprisoned by officials while a vacillating king Zedekiah privately respects yet fails to protect him. Herod's fearing and gladly hearing John yet failing to save him mirrors the weak-king-and-imprisoned-prophet dynamic. Faint and contested.

echoes.text: The fear of man proves to be a snare, but whoever puts his trust in Yahweh is kept safe.
echoes.note: The fear of human opinion becomes a snare. Herod's capitulation 'for the sake of his oaths and of his dinner guests' illustrates this proverbial snare of social fear. Wisdom-thematic resonance only; contested.

echoes.text: Jephthah vowed a vow to Yahweh, and said, “If you will indeed deliver the children of Ammon into my hand, then it shall be, that whatever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, it shall be Yahweh’s, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering.” So Jephthah passed over to the children of Ammon to fight against them; and Yahweh delivered them into his hand. He struck them from Aroer until you come […]
echoes.note: Jephthah's rash vow forces him to a deadly act he regrets, the king-bound-by-his-oath tragedy. Herod, 'exceedingly sorry' yet bound 'for the sake of his oaths,' replays this rash-vow type. Contested, thematic and structural parallel without verbal link.

echoes.text: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cup bearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants. He restored the chief cup bearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand; but he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.
echoes.note: Pharaoh's birthday feast becomes the occasion of an execution, the only other clear OT royal birthday banquet ending in death. Herod's birthday supper culminating in beheading faintly recalls this. Low confidence, contested resonance.

lines: The earth is the Lord's and all that is in it.
The world, and all who dwell therein.
David danced before the Lord with all his might.
We come with timbrel and song to meet our God.
Lift up your heads, O gates; open wide, ancient doors.
Let the King of glory come in.
Who is this King of glory? Come, let us worship.
The Lord of hosts, the King of glory. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: The whole earth belongs to God, who set it on the seas; so who may climb the holy hill and stand in that high place?
Lift up your heads, O gates!
David and all the house of Israel came dancing before the Lord with songs and lyres and tambourines, leaping with all their might.
Lift up your heads, O gates!
Throw the doors back on their hinges, fling the ancient gates wide; the King of glory is coming through, strong and mighty.
Lift up your heads, O gates!
Clean hands, honest hearts, come and climb the hill; the One we have waited for is already at the door.
Lift up your heads, O gates, and let the King of glory in!
